overview.headline: Free fall motion under constant gravity with velocity and displacement relations

keyPoints.point: Free falling defined as motion only because of gravity and described by Newtonian motion laws
keyPoints.quote: is said to be free falling and its motion is described by Newton’s second law of motion.

keyPoints.point: Acceleration is constant and equal to gravitational acceleration at sea level
keyPoints.quote: The acceleration is constant and equal to the gravitational acceleration g which is 9.8 meters per square second at sea level on the Earth.

keyPoints.point: Weight size and shape are not a factor in describing free fall
keyPoints.quote: The weight, size, and shape of the object are not a factor in describing a free fall.

keyPoints.point: Knowing acceleration we can determine velocity and location at any time
keyPoints.quote: Knowing the acceleration, we can determine the velocity and location of any free falling object at any time using the following equations.

keyTerms.gloss: external force expressed as weight acting on object in vacuum
keyTerms.quote: An object that falls through a vacuum is subjected to only one external force, the gravitational force, expressed as the weight of the object.

keyTerms.gloss: constant gravitational acceleration causing steady change in velocity
keyTerms.quote: The acceleration is constant and equal to the gravitational acceleration g which is 9.8 meters per square second at sea level on the Earth.

keyTerms.gloss: velocity determined from acceleration and time showing motion change
keyTerms.quote: Knowing the acceleration, we can determine the velocity and location of any free falling object at any time using the following equations.

keyTerms.gloss: displacement from initial location linked to acceleration
keyTerms.quote: where a is the acceleration, V is the velocity, and X is the displacement from an initial location.

keyTerms.gloss: additional drag force acting through atmosphere complicating motion description
keyTerms.quote: there is an additional drag force acting on the object and the physics involved with describing the motion of the object is more complex
